name: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome due to CDKN1C Mutation

criteria.description: Lateralized overgrowth (hemihyperplasia) of body or limbs
Abdominal wall defects such as omphalocele or umbilical hernia
Positive family history of BWS with confirmed CDKN1C mutation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diagnosis requires presence of at least two major criteria or one major plus two minor criteria, supported by genetic confirmation of CDKN1C mutation.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for CDKN1C mutations is critical for confirmation, especially in familial cases.

pathognomonic.notes: Often causes feeding and respiratory difficulties in neonates
Asymmetric growth of one side of the body or limbs
searchTerms: unequal body size on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal wall defects (omphalocele or umbilical hernia)
pathognomonic.notes: Visible defect at birth involving the abdominal wall
searchTerms: belly wall defect with organs outside

common.notes: Characteristic preauricular skin tags or creases
searchTerms: folds or pits on outer ear
ear creases or small indentations near ear

common.notes: Includes hepatomegaly, nephromegaly, and pancreatic enlargement
searchTerms: big liver, spleen, or other organs

common.notes: Excess amniotic fluid often detected prenatally
searchTerms: too much amniotic fluid in pregnancy
excess fluid around fetus before birth

occasional.notes: Enlargement of the heart detected by imaging

rare.notes: Due to macroglossia or other airway obstruction
Rare malignant liver tumor associated with BWS

laboratory: Hypoglycemia detected by blood glucose measurement
imaging: Ultrasound showing organomegaly and abdominal wall defects
Renal ultrasound for Wilms tumor screening
MRI or CT for tumor surveillance
other: Prenatal ultrasound findings of polyhydramnios and macrosomia
Physical examination revealing characteristic ear creases and macroglossia

distinguishingFeatures: Distinct facial features including coarse face and supernumerary nipples
Characteristic facial gestalt with prominent forehead

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging abdominal mass suggestive of Wilms tumor
Persistent neonatal hypoglycemia refractory to treatment
references: Weksberg R, Shuman C, Beckwith JB. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Eur J Hum Genet. 2010;18(1):8-14.
Brioude F, et al. Expert consensus document: Clinical and molecular diagnosis, screening and management of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2018;14(4):229-249.
